Selfie Stick
SEL-fee STIK
noun (Millennial slang)
An extendable pole for holding a camera or phone at arm’s-plus length to take a self-portrait. A 1983 Japanese patent by Hiroshi Ueda and Yujiro Mima of Minolta described an "extender" for compact cameras; Wayne Fromm’s Quik Pod (2005) refined it. The name selfie stick followed selfie (Oxford Dictionaries Word of the Year, 2013), and in 2014 the device was everywhere: Time named it one of the year’s best inventions. In 2015 Disney parks, many museums, and stadiums banned it for safety and courtesy.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A selfie stick is a pole that lets a person photograph himself from further away, getting the landmark, the crowd, or the friends into the frame with him at the centre. The device was briefly the emblem of the Millennial tourist: at the Colosseum, the Grand Canyon, the Sistine Chapel, a forest of poles pointed back at their owners. The Christian observation: a gadget is not a sin, and a group photo on a family trip is a good memory. But the selfie stick is a striking picture of a posture of soul. It literally extends a person’s reach so that he can turn his back on the wonder and put himself in front of it. Paul foresaw an age when "men shall be lovers of their own selves" (2Ti 3:2), and the cure he preached was a different orientation: "Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others" (Php 2:4). John the Baptist, seeing Jesus, said the sentence that is the opposite of the selfie stick: "He must increase, but I must decrease" (Joh 3:30). The Psalmist turns the camera away: "Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory" (Psa 115:1). A father on vacation takes his pictures and then puts the phone away and makes his children look: at the canyon, the cathedral, the ocean, and the God who made the eye that sees them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial-era gadget (patent 1983; craze 2014; banned at many venues 2015) for extended self-portraits; harmless as a tool, an emblem of the self put in front of every wonder (2Ti 3:2; Joh 3:30).

Webster (1828), root stick: STICK, noun [G. This word is connected with the verb to stick with stock, stack, and other words having the like elements. The primary sense of the root is to thrust, to shoot, and to set.] 1. The small shoot or branch of a tree or shrub, cut off; a rod; also, a staff; as, to strike one with a stick 2. Any stem of a tree, of any size, cut for fuel or timber. It is applied in America to any long and slender piece of timber, round or square, from the smallest size to the largest, used in the frames of buildings; […]

Decode for parents: on your next trip, count how many photos face the wonder and how many face your children; then turn some around.

Modern Corruption

The selfie stick extends the self in front of every wonder; harmless as a tool, it pictures the age of lovers of their own selves, which the Baptist answers: He must increase.

expand to see more

The corruption is not the pole but the reflex it serves: experience as a backdrop for self-documentation. At the great sights of the world, crowds now stand with their backs to the thing they travelled to see, arranging themselves in front of it. The habit trains attention inward. Even worship is now photographed from the pew. The love of self that Paul lists first among the marks of the last days needs no stick, but it was never more conveniently equipped.

The recovery is wonder that forgets itself. "When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him?" (Psa 8:3-4). That is the posture of a man looking outward and upward, and it makes the self smaller and happier. Teach children to look long at what they came to see, to photograph it if they like, and to stand in front of it less often than they stand in awe of it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English sticca (stick) + selfie (2002, Australian; Oxford WOTY 2013) → 1983 Minolta "extender" patent → 2005 Quik Pod → 2014 craze → 2015 bans.
